::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [spring 1839]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  This fragment printed by Coleridge, <i>Life</i>, 140.
:::

[To [Anne](people/person_1582.qmd)]  I am going to Hursley to-day to stay with [Mr. Keble](people/person_798.qmd), in the hopes of hastening the departure of this tiresome cold.[^1]  I like the thought of the visit very much, though it being the first time of my staying out by myself, how I shall manage winding up my watch remains to be proved.

---

[^1]: ‘A lingering cough, in the spring of 1839, led to my spending a fortnight at the Vicarage;  and this rendered it altogether another home, where for twenty-seven years every joy and care were alike carried to those who could “make grief less bitter, joy less wild.”‘   *Musings over the Christian Year*, vi.  (The quotation is from a poem which CMY made the epigraph to *The Daisy Chain*, Chapter 14: and described there as ‘Lines on a Monument at Lichfield’.)
